hints: Over which length does gravity act, and over which does friction act? Balance their work.
worded:
1. As in the previous problem, take part BC as smooth (only AC is said to have friction).

2. Gravity works over the whole length 3L (with AC = L); friction only over L.

3. From rest to rest: mg sin θ × 3L = μmg cos θ × L, so μ = 3 tan θ and k = 3. (C)
conventional:
![](asset:P000557-sol-1)

Let $AC = L$, $BC = 2L$, BC smooth.

$$mg\sin\theta(3L) - \mu mg\cos\theta(L) = 0\mkern6mu  \Rightarrow \mkern6mu \mu = 3\tan\theta,\quad k = 3.$$
mistakes: Gravity acts over the full 3L, friction only over L.
BC is taken as smooth; the problem implies it but does not say so.
